statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. The latest delayed NQ evidence available before cutoff shows continued downside extension and near-low holding, while rate, oil and prior-session semiconductor weakness remain aligned stress amplifiers.
recommendation: Current Tail is in the elevated band. The mapped policy state remains BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES while the latest observed path is near a fresh session low; a sustained reclaim with meaningful retracements would reduce the evidence for persistent mean-reversion failure.
headline: Latest delayed NQ holds near a fresh overnight low; Tail remains elevated.
body: The latest explicitly timestamped delayed December NQ quote found before cutoff was 30,523.00 at 07:04 UTC, down 0.79%, with a 30,512.75-30,713.50 session range. U.S. 10-year yields were near 5.12%, Brent remained above $102, and VIX futures were near 17.8. No sufficiently fresh sub-hour NQ path after 07:04 UTC was verified, limiting confidence in a further Tail escalation.

lookbackSummary: Tail was low early on September 23, rose into elevated territory during the U.S. selloff, de-escalated as mean reversion returned, then climbed back through WATCH overnight. The 07:00 UTC assessment reached Tail 29 as renewed downside extension held near a fresh session low.
outlookSummary: The latest delayed path remains concerning but is not fresh enough to justify assuming further current-hour extension. The strongest later conditional window is 12:00-15:15 UTC around U.S. data, Fed remarks and the cash-open sequence; higher Tail requires observed one-way continuation with weak retracements.

forecast.analysis: Latest delayed December NQ evidence available before cutoff showed 30,523.00 at 07:04 UTC, down 0.79% and only about 10 points above a 30,512.75 session low. The lower-low path, 10-year yield near 5.12%, Brent above $102 and weak semiconductor breadth keep Tail elevated, although no fresher sub-hour NQ path was verified.
drivers: Latest delayed NQ quote near a fresh session low

news.title: U.S. stock futures dip after high yields batter tech; Trump-Xi summit begins

forecast.analysis: If NQ remains near the overnight low and rebounds stay shallow, Tail would remain elevated; a sustained reclaim into the earlier 30,650-30,700 area with two-way rotations would weaken the one-way-path evidence. No future continuation is assumed.
drivers: Retracement depth after the earlier breakdown
Rates remain an amplifier only if NQ stays directionally efficient

forecast.analysis: Late European morning is modeled elevated only if repeated attempts to rebound fail and price keeps revisiting the session extreme. A durable recovery away from the low would support de-escalation before the U.S. event cluster.
drivers: Repeated rebound failures versus broader rotations

forecast.analysis: Into the pre-data lull, Tail is modeled at the low edge of the elevated band. The key conditional test is whether meaningful retracements reappear rather than another extension that holds close to fresh lows.
drivers: No assumption of a future directional break

forecast.analysis: Jobless claims and BEA international-accounts data at 12:30 UTC, followed by Hammack at 12:50, raise event Stress. Tail reaches the elevated band only conditionally if the observed post-release NQ path extends persistently with weak retracements.
drivers: Jobless claims and BEA data at 12:30 UTC
Beth Hammack opening remarks at 12:50 UTC

forecast.analysis: In the hour before the U.S. cash open, Tail is high only under a conditional path of continued post-data extension, failed retracements and aligned rates/volatility. Orderly two-way discovery would imply a lower score.
drivers: Cross-asset alignment after the 12:30 UTC releases

forecast.analysis: The cash-open hour also contains New Residential Sales at 14:00 UTC and a Williams keynote at 14:50 UTC. High Tail is conditional on actual opening-auction continuation, session-extreme holding and shallow pullbacks; event importance alone does not establish Tail.

Early cash-session follow-through remains a high conditional window if the opening impulse repeatedly extends after failed retracements. A meaningful counter-move and cooling cross-assets would reduce the modeled path risk.
By 16:00 UTC, Tail is modeled back to elevated if directional pressure persists but retracements begin to broaden. Continued near-extreme holding without recovery would invalidate that moderation.
drivers: Persistence of any opening directional impulse

forecast.analysis: The 17:00 UTC hour retains elevated conditional Tail because rate-sensitive technology can remain vulnerable after a weak open. The score assumes neither a second leg nor a reversal; actual retracement quality is the checkpoint.
drivers: Second-leg continuation is conditional, not assumed

forecast.analysis: Into the U.S. afternoon, Tail is modeled modestly elevated only if earlier directional pressure still controls the tape. Repeated two-way rotations would shift the regime toward mixed rather than trend-down.
By 19:00 UTC, WATCH is the base case if the session develops meaningful mean reversion. A fresh directional extension with little retracement would invalidate the de-escalation.
drivers: Fresh-extreme break is the re-escalation condition

forecast.analysis: Late-session Tail remains in WATCH under a mixed path. A renewed session-extreme break would be the main condition for re-escalation; otherwise the earlier event impulse should be increasingly absorbed.
At 21:00 UTC, the forecast assumes no new one-way evidence and therefore keeps Tail in WATCH. Persistent late-session continuation would be the contrary condition.
After the U.S. cash close, Tail is modeled at the bottom of WATCH as liquidity thins. The score would rise only if futures retain a strong directional imbalance rather than stabilizing.

At 23:00 UTC, the base case is low Tail if post-close futures are orderly and earlier directional pressure has not produced a new extension. Stress stays high because the rates and geopolitical backdrop can remain unsettled.
drivers: Persistent macro Stress without automatic Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: During early Asia hours, low Tail assumes balanced futures trading rather than a fresh continuation leg. Cross-asset stress can remain elevated without implying mean-reversion failure.
drivers: No carry-forward assumption from the U.S. session

forecast.analysis: At 01:00 UTC, low Tail persists conditionally if overnight trading remains two-sided. A new session gap or sustained extreme-holding would be the main reason to reassess higher.
drivers: Cross-asset alignment only matters with price-path confirmation

forecast.analysis: At 02:00 UTC, the baseline remains low Tail with normal overnight structure. The score does not assume that prior U.S. weakness continues into Asia.
drivers: Fresh extension with weak retracements would invalidate the low-Tail base case

forecast.analysis: At 03:00 UTC, low Tail continues if Asia-Europe handoff remains orderly. A renewed directional break with weak retracements would be the relevant invalidation.
At 04:00 UTC, Tail edges higher within the low band as European liquidity develops. The modeled increase reflects transition risk, not an assumed trend.
drivers: Rates and oil remain background amplifiers

forecast.analysis: At 05:00 UTC, low Tail remains the base case if European price discovery stays rotational. Persistent yields pressure would matter more if paired with renewed NQ extension.
drivers: Persistent yields pressure needs NQ confirmation

forecast.analysis: At 06:00 UTC, WATCH begins only as the next U.S. event day approaches and liquidity deepens; the score still requires observed one-way structure before any stronger action band.
drivers: Next U.S. event day approaches without a pre-release Tail assumption

forecast.analysis: At 07:00 UTC, WATCH remains a conditional pre-event posture. Durable-goods data are later at 12:30 UTC, so this slot does not assume a release outcome or pre-price a directional reaction.
drivers: Durable-goods release is later at 12:30 UTC
Pre-event structure remains the key conditional checkpoint

forecastDetail.comment: Latest delayed NQ remained near a fresh overnight low; current Tail stays elevated, with freshness limitations preventing a stronger conclusion.
Elevated Tail persists conditionally if low-holding and shallow rebounds continue; a sustained reclaim would weaken the case.
European follow-through remains the test: repeated rebound failure supports elevation, while broader rotations support de-escalation.
Pre-data Tail sits at the elevated threshold; meaningful retracements versus renewed extension determine the next move.
The 12:30 UTC data and 12:50 UTC Hammack remarks raise Stress; elevated Tail requires observed post-release one-way structure.
High Tail is conditional on persistent post-data extension and failed retracements into the cash-open approach.
